title: OU Football vs New Mexico Live: Week 3 Score, Highlights & Play‑by‑Play Updates – The Oklahoman
body:
The Oklahoma Sooners secured a hard‑fought 24‑17 victory over the New Mexico Lobos on Saturday night, snapping a two‑game losing streak and re‑establishing themselves as early contenders in the 2026 college‑football season. Quarterback Caleb “C.J.” Jensen led the charge with three touchdown passes and a clutch 22‑yard scramble in the fourth quarter, while the defense forced two critical turnovers that halted New Mexico’s momentum and preserved the win. The triumph, achieved in front of a raucous home crowd at Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium, moves the Sooners to a 2‑1 record and restores confidence in head coach Ryan Caldwell’s revamped offensive scheme.

The game’s pivotal moment arrived early in the second quarter when New Mexico’s running back Antonio “Turbo” Ramos broke free for a 34‑yard touchdown, giving the Lobos a 10‑7 lead. However, the Sooners responded on the ensuing drive, capitalizing on a blown coverage by New Mexico safety Malik Torres. Jensen connected with wide receiver Malik “Mack” Turner for a 45‑yard strike that set up a 7‑yard touchdown run by senior running back Jalen “Jet” Brooks. The Sooners reclaimed the lead 14‑10, a margin they would not relinquish despite New Mexico’s persistent attacks.

Defensive adjustments proved decisive as the second half unfolded. Early in the third quarter, sophomore cornerback Darius “D‑Man” Hall intercepted a deep pass from Lobos quarterback John Mateer, returning it to the 20‑yard line and setting up a short field goal that extended Oklahoma’s advantage to 17‑10. Hall’s second interception came with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, a pick‑six that turned a potential New Mexico rally into a decisive blow. The turnover not only halted a drive that had brought the Lobos to Oklahoma’s 35‑yard line but also added six points to the scoreboard, pushing the lead to 24‑10.

New Mexico’s offense, while occasionally explosive, struggled with consistency. Mateer, a dual‑threat quarterback, threw for 298 yards and a touchdown but was plagued by three interceptions—two of them directly resulting in points for Oklahoma. The Lobos managed to claw back a late‑game field goal, narrowing the deficit to 24‑17, but a missed fourth‑down conversion deep in their own territory sealed their fate. Analysts noted that New Mexico’s reliance on deep passing attempts left them vulnerable to Oklahoma’s aggressive secondary, a factor that will likely be addressed in the Lobos’ upcoming practice sessions.

For the Sooners, the win validates the strategic shift Caldwell implemented during the offseason, emphasizing a balanced attack that blends a power‑running game with vertical passing routes. Jensen’s poise under pressure, highlighted by his 22‑yard scramble on a third‑and‑long situation in the final quarter, underscores his development as a leader. Meanwhile, the defense’s ability to generate turnovers—totaling four forced fumbles and two interceptions—demonstrates a renewed emphasis on opportunistic playmaking. The performance also bodes well for the Sooners’ upcoming conference slate, where they will face perennial powerhouses Texas and Kansas State.

Looking ahead, Oklahoma’s next challenge arrives on the road against the Texas Longhorns, a matchup that will test the Sooners’ resilience and adaptability. If the team can maintain the defensive aggression and offensive versatility displayed against New Mexico, they stand a strong chance of contending for the Big 12 title. Conversely, New Mexico returns to the desert for a home game against the Utah State Aggies, where they must tighten ball security and improve red‑zone efficiency if they hope to rebound from this setback. Both programs will carry the lessons from Saturday night’s contest into their forthcoming battles, shaping the early narrative of the 2026 college‑football season.
